cross_cutting_boundaries.detail: EncodedCopyOverhead bounds copies of an externally supplied trace, but no reviewed graph body supplies the full trace/global reached-value invariant needed to apply it. Borrowed Input, table, label tails, retained recursion frames and held outputs remain outside the local structural charges.

flagTable, maskValue, tableValue and encoding maps are observations. BinaryPortWeightPreparation uses native Vector reads and tabulate; its operations result is not a replacement proof for those reads or bit-sized array allocation. BinaryPortMaterialization closes port labels/matrix/mask only from already retained original adjacency/low-mask Values.

Exact bridges permit joins, but the 14-module cohort does not define and certify a single charged executable from original encoded weighted input through preparation, shortcut construction, survivor restriction, survivor count/weight/cost gathering and replica/chain assembly.

Exec relations bind named recursive Boolean/list bodies to ghost local Nat counters. They do not establish the cost of computing the counters themselves, Lean compiler/native execution, heap/physical allocator behavior, or final paper runtime. Output-size bounds are not by themselves live-storage or whole-trace bounds.

Refinement uses valid numeric labels, complete ordered enumeration and represented Boolean storage; width claims track actual stored lengths, including padding. BinaryPortDecode is intentionally not a complete range validator. Short-circuit success does not certify unused malformed storage.

Semantic acceptance is conditional on the independent compilation/kernel/axiom/runtime gates. The candidate manifest explicitly reports no dedicated integrated new graph-execution regression. Baseline runtime success cannot be transferred to these 14 additions.

Original vertex count n, permanent-port count 3*n and arbitrary padded word width are kept separate. No reviewed module substitutes a transformed dimension for the original-n envelope.
